newsitem.title: USA: Final Timan Pechora approval seen in early 1997.
newsitem.headline: Final Timan Pechora approval seen in early 1997.

text.p: Texaco Inc said Monday final approval of the Timan Pechora Co production sharing agreement is expected early next year now that the remaining issues have been resolved.

It released a Timan Pechora statement that a protocol has been signed with the Special Delegation of the Russian Federation signifying completion of negotiations and mutual agreement on the text of a production sharing agreement for the project, which covers a 7,310-square-kilometer contract area about 1,800 kilometers northeast of Moscow in the Nenetsky Autonomous Okrug.

The contract area has potential recoverable reserves of 306 million tons (2.2 billion barrels) of oil, Timan Pechora said. It is estimated that a capital investment of about $20 billion will be required over the life of the project.

Timan Pechora was formed in 1994 and is owned by affiliates of Texaco and Exxon Corp, which have 30 percent each; and Amoco Corp and Norsk Hydro A/S with 20 percent each. It has agreed to a Russian participation of 20 percent and talks are under way for the inclusion of Rosneft and Arkhangelskgeoldobycha as the Russian participants.

"We have resolved the remaining issues, and the draft PSA now will be submitted to the Government of the Russian Federation, the Nenetsky Okrug, and the Arkhangelsk Oblast for review and approval," the statement said.
In the interim, Timan Pechora said, it will begin a work program involving the testing of existing wells at the Roman Trebsa field.

Once the agreement is signed, an expanded work program of civil construction and field evaluation will begin. Once it is fully effective, the contract area will be appraised by the drilling of new wells, acquisition of seismic data, and evaluation studies, which could lead to commercial declaration and full contract area development."
